content.text: {"route":"gap","reason":"Complainant raised specific omissions before the final decision and the Agency did not cure them. Subordinate-2, who allegedly used \"mothering\" and left the post, was never interviewed. Subordinate-3 may have used another demeaning term and was not interviewed. HR-2, to whom Complainant says she complained, was not interviewed. These witnesses go directly to the Agency's findings that the term was used only once, that no other demeaning language appeared in the record, and that management did not ignore her complaints. The decision also rests on a factual error, a written apology from the IPO that the record does not show. No comparator or workload data support the finding that the May 2020 tasks were routine, and the IPO's estimates of how long the tasks would take went untested."}
